newsitem.title: LEBANON: Civilian wounded in bomb blast in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Civilian wounded in bomb blast in south Lebanon.

text.p: A roadside bomb exploded in south Lebanon on Sunday, wounding a civilian motorist, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
The South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said the bomb went off near the town of Jezzine in an area north of a border zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon but under Israeli control.
It was not immediately known who was behind the blast.
Hours later, a second roadside bomb blew up as an SLA patrol passed near the village of Kfar Falous, some 12 km (eight miles) west of Jezzine, but no one was hurt, SLA sources said.
In Beirut, a spokesman for the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) said its guerrillas set off a bomb in an SLA military vehicle at Kfar Falous, killing or wounding its crew.
He said other guerrillas fired mortar bombs at an SLA outpost near Kfar Falous.

Hizobllah leads a guerrilla war against Israeli and SLA forces in a bid to drive them out from south Lebanon. Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA patrol the zone to stop cross-frontier raids on northern Israel.
